answer: With k coordinated identities, correlated equivocation exposes up to k(k−1)/2 identity pairs, so the penalty grows as O(k²), rather than as isolated per-node fines. Bonded collateral escrows make that liability collectible, while asymmetric capital depreciation and an exponential detection multiplier make a larger sybil swarm suffer sharply greater capital loss when coordination is proven. Quartz, lotus, and prism describe distinct evidence labels, not ways to dilute shared accountability.
